title: The Atlas's Immutable Documents are amendable right up until the Endgame State, then locked forever
content:
The Action Tenet at A.1.11.2.1.1.0.4.1 states the current position without hedging: "Currently, in the transition to Endgame, the Immutable Documents (Articles and Sections) can be amended pursuant to [the Weekly Governance Cycle] and [the Monthly Governance Cycle]. Once the Sky Ecosystem enters the Endgame State, the Immutable Documents of the Atlas will be forever locked down and cannot be changed."

So "Immutable" names a *destination*, not a present property. Until the switch flips, the supposedly fixed layer moves through the same cycles as everything else — the only difference between Immutable and Adaptive Documents today is what will happen to them later.

This is a deliberate bet about sequencing. Locking the core before it is right would enshrine mistakes permanently; leaving it unlocked indefinitely would make immutability rhetorical. The Atlas chooses a one-way transition and accepts a window in which its strongest guarantee is unenforced.

The consequence is that the constraint doing real work during the transition is not immutability but the substantive limit stated in A.1.11.2.1.1 and A.1.12.2: "Atlas Edits must always adhere to the Spirit of the Atlas and remain within the bounds of Universal Alignment." Until the Endgame State, the core is protected by an alignment standard and a Facilitator's judgment rather than by code.
description: During the transition, Articles and Sections can be changed through the Weekly and Monthly Cycles; entry into the Endgame State converts them into a permanently fixed core.
